domain: water security / reservoir storage monitoring (dam-level weekly hydrology panel)
prediction_question: For a listed South African dam, given the weekly storage series published through week W (DWS State of Reservoirs bulletin / NIWIS export), will that dam's storage fall below a per-dam drought threshold (e.g. % of full supply capacity, or absolute storage) at any point in the next 4 weeks? Prospective users: municipal water departments (restriction timing), irrigation boards and agri insurers (planting/coverage decisions), and the DWS's own weekly briefing cycle. A useful prediction supports earlier restriction and allocation decisions than the week-lag bulletin alone.
prediction_time: Not yet fixed. The natural instant is the publication of the weekly State of Reservoirs bulletin (typically Tuesday/Wednesday per reservoirs.earth's transparency review and DWS media releases); features would be the dam-week storage/level series through bulletin W. This instant was NOT verified from the publisher this session: the publisher's site is unreachable from this coordinator (see measurements), so release cadence is third-party-attributed, not measured. Unresolved while parked.
target_definition: Hypothetical while parked: binary per-dam 4-week-ahead storage-threshold exceedance (label source = the dam's own storage/level series, excludable from features). No official threshold table (per-dam drought/restriction levels) was obtainable this session; the threshold would be fixed from training data (as in other exceedance candidates) or from an obtainable official document. Never constructed; no split counts exist.

No South African national open-data licence instrument was found to cover DWS: data.gov.za (the national portal that would carry per-dataset licences) no longer resolves (DNS 'temporary failure in name resolution', 2026-10-23). The ZA precedent in this repo (za-municipal-audit-opinion, ready) relies on National Treasury's own terms, which do not extend to DWS.
split_strategy: Never measured. The task needs per-dam weekly series long enough for disjoint train/eval/holdout windows with drought exceedance positives in each. Third-party evidence (reservoirs.earth, read 2026-10-23) says NIWIS carries ~5 years of weekly series over ~250 listed dams; whether the HTML/PDF bulletin archive extends further back is unmeasured (site unreachable). Positives would cluster in multi-dam drought episodes (2017-2018 Western Cape 'Day Zero'; subsequent Eastern Cape/Karoo droughts), so clustered counts per window are required before any ready verdict - none were computed.

measurements.cape_town_variant_assessment: Cape-Town-only (City of Cape Town, reachable): rejected as a standalone task on split-capacity + prior-art grounds without further probing. The single supply system concentrates drought exceedance positives in the 2017-2018 'Day Zero' episode (current levels are 74.0% total and recovered), so later eval/holdout windows would likely lack positives; and the system is already the subject of published forecasting work and raw-data mirrors (Day Zero studies; Kaggle Cape Town dam-level mirrors - to be formally checked via check-novelty.py only if this variant is ever reopened).

rejection_reason: PARK (two stacked blockers, both recorded as measurements; neither is a scientific rejection of the data). (1) Access: the publisher is unreachable from this coordinator - dws.gov.za and niwis.dws.gov.za both fail (403/timeout) for a plain client and a real browser, and no Wayback capture exists of the bulletin or terms pages, so nothing about schema, history depth or terms could be measured first-hand. The same 403 may or may not apply from a Hetzner worker network (untested). (2) Licence: no redistribution terms could be read from any instrument (site blocked; data.gov.za gone; no archive capture). Under the standing rule this stays parked rather than probed further from the coordinator: an unread licence is a blocker and inventing a grant is forbidden. The Cape-Town-only fallback was assessed and rejected (single system, clustered positives, existing prior art). Access failure is not evidence the source is unusable - it is the recorded reason nothing further was measured.
review: The strongest task idea of the 2026-10-23 Africa tick (national per-dam drought early warning, ~250 dams, weekly, real decision value for restrictions and irrigation) parked on two measured blockers before any costly probing. Everything currently attributed to the source is third-party and must be re-measured. The cheap decisive probes are named in next_action and are worth one bounded attempt per future tick.
